entries.before: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
entries.after: He had a dragon countenance and plaque-like teeth, and stood seven chi eight cun tall.
entries.sourceQuote: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
entries.sourceReason: 龍顏版齒 is dragon countenance and plaque teeth; 七尺八寸 are chi and cun, not English feet and inches.

entries.before: Huang killed Zhao, sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation, met Ren at Xiandu.
entries.after: Huang killed Zhao and sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation; they met Ren at Xiandu.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝殺昭，遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆。
entries.sourceReason: 遇仁於險瀆 follows 遣使按檢: the envoys met Ren at Xiandu, not an ambiguous subject that could read as Huang.

entries.before: Ren saw his plot exposed, killed the messenger, and fled east to Pingguo.
entries.after: Ren knew the affair had come out; he killed Huang’s envoy and returned east to Pingguo.
entries.sourceQuote: 仁知事發，殺皝使，東歸平郭。
entries.sourceReason: 東歸平郭 is returning east to Pingguo, not merely fleeing east; 知事發 is knowing the affair had broken.

entries.before: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and other Xianbei chiefs backed him.
entries.after: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all backed him.
entries.sourceQuote: 宇文歸、段遼及鮮卑諸部並為之援，
entries.sourceReason: 鮮卑諸部 means the various Xianbei divisions or tribes, not “other Xianbei chiefs.”

entries.before: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent Marshal Feng Yi to strike the Xianbei leader Muti at Bailang and Shuyu to strike the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both enemy heads were taken.
entries.after: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent his marshal Feng Yi to attack the Xianbei Muti at Bailang, and the Yangwei general Shuyu to attack the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both were beheaded.
entries.sourceQuote: 咸和九年，皝遣其司馬封弈攻鮮卑木堤于白狼，揚威淑虞攻烏丸悉羅侯于平岡，皆斬之。
entries.sourceReason: EN drops the 揚威 title before 淑虞 and understates 皆斬之 as taking heads without the paired beheading.

entries.before: Duan Lan and Murong Han attacked Liucheng until commandant Shi Cong drove them off.
entries.after: Liao’s younger brother Lan together with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.
entries.sourceQuote: 遼弟蘭與翰寇柳城，都尉石琮擊敗之。
entries.sourceReason: 遼弟蘭 marks Lan as Liao’s younger brother; 寇/擊敗 are raid and defeat, not a vague ‘until driven off.’

entries.before: Huang warned Murong Han (the general of pacifying distance): “The foe is numerous and keen—do not trade blows rashly; wait until your force is formed, then attack.”
entries.after: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is numerous and their spirit keen; it is hard to contend at the spear-tip. You ought to look to complete safety, and carefully do not advance lightly; you must wait until the troops are gathered and the lines set, then strike them.”
entries.sourceQuote: 皝戒汗曰：「賊眾氣銳，難與爭鋒，宜顧萬全，慎勿輕進，必須兵集陣整，然後擊之。」
entries.sourceReason: The supplied EN quote omits 難與爭鋒, 宜顧萬全, and 慎勿輕進 as distinct admonitions in Huang’s warning.

entries.before: Murong Han was impetuous: he sent a thousand horse ahead as a van, ignored Feng Yi’s warning, and was routed by Duan Lan with heavy losses.
entries.after: Han’s nature was fierce and keen; he dispatched over a thousand cavalry as a vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him, but Han did not follow, was defeated by Lan, and the dead were more than half.
entries.sourceQuote: 汗性驍銳，遣千餘騎為前鋒而進，封弈止之，汗不從，為蘭所敗，死者大半。
entries.sourceReason: 千餘騎 is over a thousand cavalry, not ‘a thousand,’ and 死者大半 is more than half dead.

entries.before: Sheyiyu led cavalry to pursue battle at Hunshui; again defeated them.
entries.after: Sheyiyu led cavalry to pursue battle at the Hun River and was again defeated.
entries.sourceQuote: 涉奕于率騎追戰于渾水，又敗之。
entries.sourceReason: 又敗之 after Feng Yi’s prior victory means Sheyiyu was again defeated, not that Sheyiyu defeated ‘them.’

entries.before: Huang replied, “This gulf seldom froze in the past, yet since Ren’s revolt it has frozen solid three winters running.
entries.after: Huang said, “Formerly the sea water had no ice; since Ren’s rebellion, the freeze has joined three times.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝曰：「舊海水無淩，自仁反已來，凍合者三矣。
entries.sourceReason: 舊海水無淩 is that the sea formerly had no ice, not that it ‘seldom froze’; 凍合者三矣 is three freezes.

entries.before: Ren never expected him: Huang’s vanguard was seven li from Pingguo before Ren learned of it; Ren scrambled into battle, was taken, and executed.
entries.after: Ren did not expect Huang’s arrival; the army was seven li from Pingguo when scout riders reported it; Ren came out to fight in confusion, was captured by Huang, who killed Ren and returned.
entries.sourceQuote: 仁不虞皝之至也，軍去平郭七里，候騎乃告，仁狼狽出戰，為皝所擒，殺仁而還。
entries.sourceReason: 軍去平郭七里 is the army, not a ‘vanguard’; EN omits 候騎乃告 and 殺仁而還.

entries.before: Duan Liao’s night raid on Wuxing failed in the rain; Zhang Meng ran down Li Yong and captured him.
entries.after: Duan Liao sent general Li Yong to night-raid Wuxing; meeting rain, he withdrew; commandant Zhang Meng pursued and captured Yong.
entries.sourceQuote: 段遼遣將李詠夜襲武興，遇雨，引還，都尉張萌追擊，擒詠。
entries.sourceReason: 遣將李詠 is Liao sending general Li Yong; EN also drops 都尉 for Zhang Meng and the withdraw-then-pursue sequence.

entries.before: Feng Yi chased with light horse, seized their supplies, and fed his men from enemy granaries for twenty days.
entries.after: He sent Feng Yi leading light cavalry in pursuit; Feng defeated them, gathered their military stores, lodged on their grain for twenty days, and returned.
entries.sourceQuote: 遣封弈率輕騎追擊，敗之，收其軍實，館穀二旬而還。
entries.sourceReason: EN omits 遣, the defeat 敗之, and the return 而還 after 館穀二旬.

entries.before: He sent Liu Bin and Yang Jing to escort Xu Meng’s party to the capital.
entries.after: He sent concurrent chief clerk Liu Bin and palace director Yang Jing to escort Xu Meng and others back to the capital.
entries.sourceQuote: 遣兼長史劉斌、郎中令陽景送徐孟等歸於京師。
entries.sourceReason: 兼長史 and 郎中令 are explicit offices for Liu Bin and Yang Jing; EN drops both roles.

entries.before: His heir Murong Jun stormed Duan Liao’s towns while Feng Yi struck the Yuwen—both returned in triumph.
entries.after: He had his heir apparent Jun campaign against Duan Liao’s cities, and Feng Yi attack a separate Yuwen division; both returned in great victory.
entries.sourceQuote: 使其世子俊伐段遼諸城，封弈攻宇文別部，皆大捷而歸。
entries.sourceReason: 攻宇文別部 is a separate Yuwen division, not undifferentiated ‘the Yuwen’; 使其/伐 structure is also flattened.

entries.before: He shifted his seat to Changli, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and stationed Lan Bo there to choke the enemy.
entries.after: He later relocated Changli commandery, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and had general Lan Bo garrison it to press Yilian.
entries.sourceQuote: 後徙昌黎郡，築好城于乙連東，使將軍蘭勃戍之，以逼乙連。
entries.sourceReason: 徙昌黎郡 relocates Changli commandery; it is not Huang shifting his own seat to Changli; EN also drops 將軍 and 以逼乙連.

entries.before: Qu Yun attacked Xingguo but Murong Zun destroyed him at Wuguan River and took his entire force.
entries.after: Liao sent general Qu Yun to attack Xingguo; Yun fought a great battle with Huang’s general Murong Zun at Wuguan River, was defeated and beheaded, and his entire force was captured.
entries.sourceQuote: 遼遣將屈雲攻興國，與皝將慕容遵大戰于五官水上，雲敗，斬之，盡俘其眾。
entries.sourceReason: 遼遣將 and 皝將 are omitted; 雲敗，斬之 is defeat then beheading, not a vague ‘destroyed.’

entries.before: He made Lady Duan queen and Murong Jun crown prince, citing Cao Cao and Sima Zhao as precedents.
entries.after: He made his wife Lady Duan queen and the heir apparent Jun crown prince, all following the Wei Wu and Jin Wen precedents of assisting in government.
entries.sourceQuote: 以其妻段氏為王后，世子俊為太子，皆如魏武、晉文輔政故事。
entries.sourceReason: 其妻 and 世子 are explicit; 輔政故事 is the assisting-government precedent, not a bare name citation.

entries.before: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not coordinated, drove on to Jicheng with hundreds of thousands of men; thirty-six towns went over to him.
entries.after: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not joined forces, advanced to strike him as far as Jicheng; several hundred thousand troops attacked from all four sides, and thirty-six cities among the prefectures, counties, and various divisions rebelled in response to Shi Hu.
entries.sourceQuote: 季龍進入令支，怒皝之不會師也，進軍擊之，至於棘城，戎卒數十萬，四面進攻，郡縣諸部叛應季龍者三十六城。
entries.sourceReason: 四面進攻 is attack from all four sides; 郡縣諸部叛應…三十六城 is prefectures, counties, and divisions, not only ‘towns.’

entries.before: Sent sons Ke and others leading cavalry two thousand, dawn sortie struck them.
entries.after: Sent his son Ke and others leading two thousand cavalry; at dawn they sortied and struck them.
entries.sourceQuote: 遣子恪等率騎二千，晨出擊之。
entries.sourceReason: 子恪等 is his son Ke and others, not plural ‘sons Ke’; 晨出擊之 is a dawn sortie that struck them.

entries.before: studied
entries.after: esteemed
entries.sourceQuote: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
entries.sourceReason: 尚經學 means Huang esteemed classical learning; ‘studied’ understates 尚 as mere study.

entries.before: Shi Hu sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
entries.after: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng against Fancheng without success but seized Guangcheng.
entries.sourceQuote: 季龍又使石成入攻凡城，不克，進陷廣城。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Shi Hu again sent Shi Cheng to attack Fancheng, failed, then advanced and took Guangcheng; EN omits again (又).

entries.before: When Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi held power, he submitted a memorial: I have studied wise and foolish rulers of past ages. When they favored the worthy and elevated them together, the realm rose to peace;
entries.after: Moreover, when Murong Huang learned that Yu Liang had died and Yu Bing and Yu Yi had succeeded as generals and ministers, he submitted a memorial: Your servant has closely observed the muddled and clear rulers of former ages; if they could treat the worthy with intimacy and elevate them together, then merit reached peaceful ascendancy;
entries.sourceQuote: 又聞庾亮薨，弟冰、翼繼為將相，乃表曰：臣究觀前代昏明之主，若能親賢並建，則功致升平；
entries.sourceReason: Source: moreover Huang learned Yu Liang died and Bing and Yi succeeded as generals-ministers, then memorialized on muddled vs clear rulers who elevate the worthy together; EN drops 又 and softens 继为将相/昏明.

entries.before: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
entries.after: If one could change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided.
entries.sourceQuote: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
entries.sourceReason: Source: if one can change course, overturn and collapse can be avoided; EN adds in time, which Chinese does not state.

entries.before: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
entries.after: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side, and recalling past affairs still burns with anguish to this day.
entries.sourceQuote: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age and should exalt Jins Way, yet meets many state hardships, with deep grief pressing and past affairs still burning; EN merges 命世天挺 into one gloss.

entries.before: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
entries.after: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.
entries.sourceQuote: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
entries.sourceReason: Source: tracing the cause, late Minister of Works Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle held heavy power, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals so Su Jun and Zu Yue ruined the state; EN adds harshly.

entries.before: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
entries.after: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
entries.sourceQuote: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
entries.sourceReason: Source: past events if not forgotten are a model for later affairs, yet Bing as Zhongshu jian and Left General with fellows holds central pivot and outer commands, brothers side by side unmatched; EN drops 不忘.

entries.before: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
entries.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and his fellows ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
entries.sourceQuote: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Your Majesty deeply honors Weiyang maternal-uncle ties; Bing and others ought themselves to stretch necks in expectation; EN replaces 渭阳 with generic family ties.

entries.before: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
entries.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
entries.sourceQuote: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Huang often asks why not enfeoff maternal clan with vassal states, enrich stipends and gifts, and limit power and advantage so there is no partial favor above or private talk below; EN turns 何不 into an imperative and drops 利.

entries.before: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
entries.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
entries.sourceQuote: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
entries.sourceReason: Source: servant and Bing and others differ in rank and are far apart in situation; as close imperial kin they warrant deference to circumstances; EN drops 等 and reorders speakers.

entries.before: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
entries.after: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold the rank of supreme general, worry day and night and know not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.
entries.sourceQuote: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
entries.sourceReason: Source: disheveled-hair foreign general worries day and night how to repay, can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, and exert strength and sincerity to answer state grace; EN truncates the closing clauses.

entries.before: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
entries.after: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant and he withdrew.
entries.sourceQuote: 其年皝伐高句麗，王釗乞盟而還。
entries.sourceReason: Source: that year Huang campaigned against Goguryeo; King Zhao begged a covenant and Huang returned; EN reduces 乞盟 to sued for peace.

entries.before: Planning against the Shi, he told his commanders, “Shi Hu trusts his garrisons at Anle and neglects the open country north and south of the wall—a sudden raid could overrun the whole Ji plain.”
entries.after: Huang was about to plan against the Shi clan; he calmly told the generals: “Shi Hu thinks the cities of Anle and the rest are strictly and heavily guarded, and surely sets no defenses north and south of the city; now if we take a deceitful route and strike where he does not expect, the whole northern territory of Ji can be broken.”
entries.sourceQuote: 皝將圖石氏，從容謂諸將曰：「石季龍自以安樂諸城守防嚴重，城之南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，冀之北土盡可破也。」
entries.sourceReason: Source: planning against the Shi, Huang calmly told generals Shi Hu trusts Anle and the other cities heavy defenses so north and south of the city lack preparations; a deceitful route unexpected could break all northern Ji; EN misstates north/south of the wall and whole Ji plain, and drops 从容/诡路.

entries.before: Emperor Cheng then sent Guo Xi to invest him as palace attendant, grand commander north of the river, grand general, and king of Yan, leaving other posts unchanged.
entries.after: Emperor Cheng then sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang Palace Attendant, Grand Commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Grand General, and King of Yan, leaving the rest of his offices as before.
entries.sourceQuote: 於是成帝使兼大鴻臚郭希持節拜皝侍中、大都督河北諸軍事、大將軍、燕王，其餘官皆如故。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Emperor Cheng sent concurrent Grand Herald Guo Xi bearing credentials to appoint Huang palace attendant, grand commander of military affairs north of the Yellow River, grand general, and King of Yan, other offices unchanged; EN drops concurrent Grand Herald and bearing credentials.

entries.before: He took forty thousand veterans through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and Murong Chui as van while Wang Yu led fifteen thousand from Beizhi.
entries.after: He took forty thousand picked soldiers through the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo, with Murong Han and his son Murong Chui as vanguard, and sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others leading fifteen thousand to advance from Beizhi.
entries.sourceQuote: 率勁卒四萬，入自南陝，以伐宇文、高句麗，又使翰及子垂為前鋒，遣長史王寓等勒眾萬五千，從北置而進。
entries.sourceReason: Source: led 40,000 picked troops in from the southern defile against Yuwen and Goguryeo; had Han and son Chui as vanguard; sent chief clerk Wang Yu and others with 15,000 advancing from Beizhi; EN drops 长史 and 等.

entries.before: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
entries.after: King Gao Zhao assumed Huang’s army was coming by the northern route, so he sent his younger brother Wu leading fifty thousand picked troops to block Beizhi, and personally led weaker troops to guard the southern defile.
entries.sourceQuote: 高句麗王釗謂皝軍之從北路也，乃遣其弟武統精銳五萬距北置，躬率弱卒以防南陝。
entries.sourceReason: Source: King Zhao thought Huang came by the northern route, so sent brother Wu with 50,000 picked troops to block Beizhi and personally led weak troops to guard the southern defile; EN drops 精锐.

entries.before: Yuwen Gui sent Moqian Hun; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
entries.after: Yuwen Gui sent his state chancellor Moqian Hun against Huang; Huang’s generals begged to fight but he refused.
entries.sourceQuote: 宇文歸遣其國相莫淺渾伐皝，諸將請戰，皝不許。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Yuwen Gui sent state chancellor Moqian Hun to campaign against Huang; generals asked to fight and Huang refused; EN omits 国相.

entries.before: Murong Huang toured his domains, pushed farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
entries.after: Murong Huang personally toured his prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised palaces at Longcheng.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝躬巡郡縣，勸課農桑，起龍城宮闕。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Huang personally toured prefectures and counties, urged farming and sericulture, and raised Longcheng palace towers; EN drops 躬.

entries.before: Yuwen Gui sent Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han; Huang sent word: “Sheyiyu is fierce—spar lightly until he grows reckless, then strike.”
entries.after: Yuwen Gui sent his cavalry general Sheyiyu to hold Murong Han with the whole host; Huang sent word at a gallop: “Sheyiyu is fierce and bold; you ought to avoid him a little, wait until the bandits grow arrogant, then take them.”
entries.sourceQuote: 歸使其騎將涉奕於盡眾距翰，皝馳遣謂翰曰：「奕於雄悍，宜小避之，待虜勢驕，然後取也。」
entries.sourceReason: Source: Gui had cavalry general Sheyiyu exhaust the host against Han; Huang sent word Sheyiyu is fierce and bold so slightly avoid him until the foe grows arrogant then take them; EN mistranslates 小避 as spar lightly.

entries.before: He attacked, slew Sheyiyu, took his army, and drove Yuwen Gui deep into the steppe.
entries.after: He then advanced to battle, beheaded Sheyiyu, and wholly captured their host; Gui fled far to the northern desert.
entries.sourceQuote: 於是前戰，斬奕於，盡俘其眾，歸遠遁漠北。
entries.sourceReason: Source: they advanced, beheaded Sheyiyu, wholly captured the host; Gui fled far to the northern desert; EN makes Huang drive him rather than Gui flee.

entries.before: He annexed a thousand li of pasture, resettled fifty thousand Yuwen dependents at Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu’s fort Weide.
entries.after: He opened over a thousand li of territory, moved more than fifty thousand of their tribal settlements to Changli, and changed Sheyiyu city to Weide city.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝開地千餘里，徙其部人五萬餘落于昌黎，改涉奕於城為威德城。
entries.sourceReason: Source: Huang opened over a thousand li, moved their division people over 50,000 settlements (落) to Changli, and renamed Sheyiyu city Weide; EN turns 落 into dependents.

entries.before: The ruler exists for his people; the people live on grain.
entries.after: The ruler takes the people as the foundation of the state; the people depend on grain for their lives.
entries.sourceQuote: 君以黎元為國，黎元以穀為命。
entries.sourceReason: 君以黎元為國 states the ruler’s dependence on the people as the state’s basis, not the different proposition that the ruler exists for the people.

entries.before: Cap tradesmen and aides to fixed quotas; everyone else goes back to the plow.
entries.after: The Four Assistants and the generals shall promptly fix quotas for artisans and merchants; the rest shall return to farming.
entries.sourceQuote: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
entries.sourceReason: 百工商賈數 is the matter to be regulated; 四佐與列將 are officials instructed to fix the quotas, not aides whose numbers are being capped.

entries.before: Hundred crafts and merchants’ numbers, four assistants and column generals quickly fix great quotas; the rest return to farming.
entries.after: As for the numbers of artisans and merchants, let the Four Assistants and the generals promptly establish the overall quotas; let the remainder return to farming.
entries.sourceQuote: 百工商賈數，四佐與列將速定大員，余者還農。
entries.sourceReason: The current literal field obscures the subject and imperative. 四佐與列將速定大員 assigns the quota-setting duty to the Four Assistants and generals.

entries.before: Strike idle students from the rolls.
entries.after: Students unable to benefit from instruction shall also be removed from the rolls.
entries.sourceQuote: 學生不任訓教者，亦除員錄。
entries.sourceReason: 不任訓教 concerns inability to receive or bear instruction; the adjective idle substitutes a judgment of diligence not stated here.

entries.before: Students who do not bear training and teaching, also remove from rolls.
entries.after: Students who are not capable of receiving instruction shall also be removed from the rolls.
entries.sourceQuote: 學生不任訓教者，亦除員錄。
entries.sourceReason: 不任訓教 does not mean students fail to bear the work of training and teaching others. The students are recipients of instruction.

entries.before: Feng Sheng staunchly upright, deeply attained the body of a royal minister.
entries.after: Master Feng is steadfastly upright and deeply embodies the character of a royal minister.
entries.sourceQuote: 封生蹇蹇，深得王臣之體。
entries.sourceReason: 封生 is an honorific designation of Feng, identified earlier in the complete linked passage as 封裕, not a personal name Feng Sheng. 王臣之體 concerns ministerial character, not a physical body.

entries.before: A black dragon and a white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang led his court within two hundred paces and offered the great sacrifice.
entries.after: At that time one black dragon and one white dragon appeared on Long Mountain; Huang personally led his officials to observe them from more than two hundred paces away and offered a sacrifice (source wording 祭乙太宰 remains uncertain and is not silently emended).
entries.sourceQuote: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。
entries.sourceReason: 去龍二百餘步 and 親率群僚觀之 are clear; 祭乙太宰 is anomalous in the supplied Chinese, so distance and observation are fixed while the sacrifice wording stays explicitly unresolved without emendation.

entries.before: At the time there were black dragon and white dragon each one, appeared at Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them, two hundred-odd steps from the dragons, sacrificed with the grand boar offering.
entries.after: At the time there were one black dragon and one white dragon, which appeared on Long Mountain; Huang personally led the group of officials to observe them at a distance of more than two hundred paces from the dragons, and performed a sacrifice (anomalous source wording 祭乙太宰 left unresolved; not read as a grand-boar offering or silent 太牢 emendation).
entries.sourceQuote: 時有黑龍、白龍各一，見於龍山，皝親率群僚觀之，去龍二百餘步，祭乙太宰。
entries.sourceReason: Literal must not render 祭乙太宰 as a grand boar or imported 太牢; correct the distance phrasing and leave the sacrifice wording unresolved.

entries.before: He labeled elite students “high-gate pupils,” reopened the eastern school for archery rites, and each month examined their progress.
entries.after: He gave the sons and younger brothers of his senior ministers who were official students the title “high-gate students,” established the eastern school in the old palace for the village archery rites, and personally observed and assessed their performance each month.
entries.sourceQuote: 賜其大臣子弟為官學生者號高門生，立東庠于舊宮，以行鄉射之禮，每月臨觀，考試優劣。
entries.sourceReason: 立東庠于舊宮 establishes a school in the old palace; it does not say reopened. The fuller wording also preserves the official-student qualification and the kinship group receiving the title.

entries.before: Because of long drought, begged off common people’s field rent.
entries.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people’s field tax.
entries.sourceQuote: 以久旱，丐百姓田租。
entries.sourceReason: 丐百姓田租 here is remission of the commoners' field rent/tax; begged off misstates the ruler's act. Independently, current en also understates 久旱 and 百姓 and is repaired separately.

entries.before: He abolished several empty commanderies such as Chengzhou, Jiyang, and Yingqiu.
entries.after: He abolished Chengzhou, Jiyang, Yingqiu, and other commanderies.
entries.sourceQuote: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡。
entries.sourceReason: 罷成周、冀陽、營丘等郡 does not describe the commanderies as empty. Remove that unsupported characterization; the literal field already preserves the unqualified abolition.

entries.before: Poor households received draft oxen to till the royal park on an eighty-twenty revenue split with the state.
entries.after: Herding oxen were given to poor families to till fields in the royal park; the state took eight-tenths, and two-tenths went to the private holders.
entries.sourceQuote: 以牧牛給貧家，田于苑中，公收其八，二分入私。
entries.sourceReason: 公收其八，二分入私 assigns eight-tenths to the public and two private; eighty-twenty with the state can reverse those shares.

entries.before: Householders who owned cattle but no land tilled the park on a seventy-thirty split.
entries.after: Those who had oxen but no land also tilled the park; the state took seven-tenths, and three-tenths went to the private holders.
entries.sourceQuote: 有牛而無地者，亦田苑中，公收其七，三分入私。
entries.sourceReason: 公收其七，三分入私 must keep public seven-tenths and private three-tenths explicit rather than an ownerless seventy-thirty split.

entries.before: he clothes the cold and feeds the hungry until every household is provided for.
entries.after: he clothes the cold and feeds the hungry so that every household is provided for and every person has enough.
entries.sourceQuote: 寒者衣之，饑者食之，使家給人足。
entries.sourceReason: 家給人足 is paired household provision and personal sufficiency; omitting 人足 drops half the result.

entries.before: Because high agricultural officers are chosen and encouragement enforced, each man tends a full hundred mu without borrowing oxen;
entries.after: Agricultural officers are carefully selected and encouragement and assessment are pressed to the utmost, so each man tends a full hundred mu without borrowing oxen;
entries.sourceQuote: 高選農官，務盡勸課，人治周田百畝，亦不假牛力；
entries.sourceReason: 高選 is careful selection of farm officers, not high-ranking officers; 勸課 includes assessment.

entries.before: those who labor receive honors and the idle are punished.
entries.after: those who labor in the fields receive honors of distinction, while idle farmers suffer the penalty of being denied peer standing.
entries.sourceQuote: 力田者受旌顯之賞，惰農者有不齒之罰。
entries.sourceReason: 旌顯之賞 and 不齒之罰 name distinctive honor and the unranked penalty, not bare honors-versus-punished.

entries.before: Offices are matched to need, men do not hold empty posts, and salaries are trimmed to yearly revenue.
entries.after: Again, assess the work to establish offices and the offices to appoint personnel, ensuring that offices meet needs and no one occupies a post in vain; estimate the annual revenue and set their salaries accordingly.
entries.sourceQuote: 又量事置官，量官置人，使官必稱須，人不虛位，度歲入多少，裁而祿之。
entries.sourceReason: 量事置官，量官置人 are separate staffing steps. 裁而祿之 sets salaries according to estimated annual revenue; it does not necessarily order salary reductions.

entries.before: Yet though farming orders issue repeatedly, no magistrate or two-thousand-bushel official works the land with public zeal.
entries.after: Yet though farming orders issue repeatedly, no two-thousand-bushel official or magistrate is intent on public diligence or keen to exhaust the land's advantage.
entries.sourceQuote: 雖務農之令屢發，二千石令長莫有志勤在公、銳盡地利者。
entries.sourceReason: 莫有志勤在公、銳盡地利者 denies both public diligence and exhausting land advantage.

entries.before: Knowing this, Han's founder executed more than ten such officials for false land reports, and under Ming and Zhang the age was nearly peaceful.
entries.after: Knowing this, Han's founder summoned and executed two-thousand-bushel officials by the tens for false reports of reclaimed fields, and under Ming and Zhang the age was called nearly peaceful.
entries.sourceQuote: 故漢祖知其如此，以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數，是以明、章之際，號次升平。
entries.sourceReason: 征殺 keeps summon-and-execute; 以十數 is counted by tens; 墾田 and 號次升平 should not be thinned away.

entries.before: Therefore Han's founder, knowing this, executed more than ten such officials for false reports of reclaimed fields, and in the Ming and Zhang era the age was called nearly peaceful.
entries.after: Therefore Han's founder, knowing this, summoned and executed two-thousand-bushel officials by the tens for false reports of reclaimed fields, and in the Ming and Zhang era the age was called nearly peaceful.
entries.sourceQuote: 故漢祖知其如此，以墾田不實，征殺二千石以十數，是以明、章之際，號次升平。
entries.sourceReason: Literal likewise needs 征 as summon before execution and 以十數 as counted by tens, not more than ten.

entries.before: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate and hunger fills the ditches.
entries.after: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, for a thousand li no smoke rises; hunger and cold bring ruin, and people fall one after another into the ditches.
entries.sourceQuote: 自永嘉喪亂，百姓流亡，中原蕭條，千里無煙，饑寒流隕，相繼溝壑。
entries.sourceReason: 千里無煙, 饑寒流隕, and 相繼溝壑 are distinct desolation propositions omitted by the abbreviated en.

entries.before: Your Highness, with heroic endowment, has extended the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li and added a hundred thousand households, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
entries.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, with achievements in following his predecessor’s footsteps and expanding the realm that surpass those of the great Earl of the West.
entries.sourceQuote: 殿下以英聖之資，克廣先業，南摧強趙，東滅句麗，開境三千，戶增十萬，繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯。
entries.sourceReason: 繼武 means following a predecessor’s footsteps, not martial expansion; 闡廣 is expansion, and 有高西伯 says the achievements surpass those of the Earl of the West.

entries.before: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the merit of martial expansion, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
entries.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, with achievements in following his predecessor’s footsteps and expanding the realm that surpass those of the great Earl of the West.
entries.sourceQuote: 殿下以英聖之資，克廣先業，南摧強趙，東滅句麗，開境三千，戶增十萬，繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯。
entries.sourceReason: 繼武 means following a predecessor’s footsteps, not martial expansion; 闡廣 is expansion, and 有高西伯 says the achievements surpass those of the Earl of the West.

entries.before: Reduce the royal parks and settle refugees on the land.
entries.after: It is fitting to reduce and abolish the parks and settle the displaced on them.
entries.sourceQuote: 宜省罷諸苑，以業流人。
entries.sourceReason: 宜省罷諸苑 requires both reduction and abolition to give livelihood to the displaced.

entries.before: Even Wei and Jin, though the Way faded, did not reduce the people below seven or eight tenths; official-ox farmers gave six parts to the state and four to the people, private-ox farmers split evenly, and all rejoiced.
entries.after: Even Wei and Jin, though the Way faded, still did not cut the people by as much as seven or eight tenths; those farming with official oxen gave six parts to the state and four to the people, those with private oxen on official land split evenly with the state, and the people were secure and all rejoiced.
entries.sourceQuote: 且魏、晉雖道消之世，猶削百姓不至於七八，持官牛田者官得六分，百姓得四分，私牛而官田者與官中分，百姓安之，人皆悅樂。
entries.sourceReason: 削百姓不至於七八 caps exaction short of 7–8/10, matching later 6/4 and 5/5; below-seven-or-eight misreads the share.

entries.before: Even Wei and Jin, though an age of fading Way, still did not reduce the people below seven or eight tenths; those who farmed with official oxen gave six parts to the state and four to the people; those with private oxen on official land split evenly with the state; the people were secure and all rejoiced.
entries.after: Even Wei and Jin, though an age of fading Way, still did not cut into the people as far as seven or eight tenths; those who farmed with official oxen gave six parts to the state and four to the people; those with private oxen on official land split evenly with the state; the people were secure and all rejoiced.
entries.sourceQuote: 且魏、晉雖道消之世，猶削百姓不至於七八，持官牛田者官得六分，百姓得四分，私牛而官田者與官中分，百姓安之，人皆悅樂。
entries.sourceReason: Same 七八 share correction as en: exaction stops short of seven or eight tenths.

entries.before: With households nearing a hundred thousand crowded against the capital, divide their kindred and move them to western border cities, ruling them with kindness and law so they do not learn the state's strength and weakness.
entries.after: Now households approach a hundred thousand, crowded against the capital; I fear this will soon become a deep harm to the state. Divide their brothers and lineage and move them to western border cities, soothe them with kindness and restrain them with law, so they do not scatter among settled people and learn the state's strength and weakness.
entries.sourceQuote: 今戶垂十萬，狹湊都城，恐方將為國家深害，宜分其兄弟宗屬，徙于西境諸城，撫之以恩，檢之以法，使不得散在居人，知國之虛實。
entries.sourceReason: 恐方將為國家深害 and 使不得散在居人，知國之虛實 are omitted or conflated in the abbreviated en.

entries.before: The central plain is not pacified and stores must grow, yet offices multiply and idlers abound; one man who does not plow makes the year hungrier.
entries.after: The central plain is not yet pacified and stores ought to be enlarged; official posts are numerous and idlers not few; when one man does not plow, hunger is suffered through the year.
entries.sourceQuote: 今中原未平，資畜宜廣，官司猥多，遊食不少，一夫不耕，歲受其饑。
entries.sourceReason: 歲受其饑 is yearlong hunger/privation consequent on one non-plower, not the year itself made hungrier.

entries.before: Now the central plain is not yet pacified and stores ought to be enlarged; official posts are numerous and idlers not few; one man who does not plow, the year receives his hunger.
entries.after: Now the central plain is not yet pacified and stores ought to be enlarged; official posts are numerous and idlers not few; when one man does not plow, hunger is suffered through the year.
entries.sourceQuote: 今中原未平，資畜宜廣，官司猥多，遊食不少，一夫不耕，歲受其饑。
entries.sourceReason: Literal year-receives-his-hunger personifies 歲; render the yearlong privation caused by one non-plower.

entries.before: Food taken from plowmen feeds idlers; tens of thousands eat without plowing, and the loss is the same; how can every household be provided for and the realm governed to peace!
entries.after: Food must be taken from those who plow to feed them; one person consumes the labor of one person, and with tens of thousands living without working, the loss is likewise in the tens of thousands; how can every household be provided for and every person have enough, and government bring about peace!
entries.sourceQuote: 必取於耕者而食之，一人食一人之力，游食數萬，損亦如之，安可以家給人足，治致升平！
entries.sourceReason: 一人食一人之力 explicitly gives the one-to-one labor burden, 損亦如之 extends it to tens of thousands, and 家給人足 requires both household provision and personal sufficiency.

entries.before: Men of world-ranging talent may be placed as needed.
entries.after: Those with world-surpassing strategy and talent matching the age's needs may be placed in posts as required.
entries.sourceQuote: 其有經略出世，才稱時求者，自可隨須置之列位。
entries.sourceReason: 經略出世 is world-surpassing/outstanding strategy, not world-ranging talent alone.

entries.before: Those with world-ranging strategy and talent suited to the age's needs may be placed in posts as needed.
entries.after: Those with world-surpassing strategy and talent matching the age's needs may be placed in posts as needed.
entries.sourceQuote: 其有經略出世，才稱時求者，自可隨須置之列位。
entries.sourceReason: Literal world-ranging understates 出世; use world-surpassing strategy with talent matching the times.

entries.before: Your Highness is broad and clear, thirsting for counsel; men speak even humble truths without hiding.
entries.after: Your Highness is sage in nature, broad and clear, thirsting for counsel as for water; therefore men fully offer even rustic woodcutter counsel, offending yet not hiding.
entries.sourceQuote: 殿下聖性寬明，思言若渴，故人盡芻蕘，有犯無隱。
entries.sourceReason: 聖性, 芻蕘 as rustic counsel, and 有犯無隱 must remain; humble truths without hiding understates them.

entries.before: Your Highness is sage in nature, broad and clear, thirsting for words as for water; therefore men exhaust even firewood and grass, offending yet not hiding.
entries.after: Your Highness is sage in nature, broad and clear, thirsting for words as for water; therefore men fully offer even the counsel of woodcutters and fuel-gatherers, offending yet not hiding.
entries.sourceQuote: 殿下聖性寬明，思言若渴，故人盡芻蕘，有犯無隱。
entries.sourceReason: 人盡芻蕘 is the idiom of exhausting humble rustic counsel, not exhausting firewood and grass as materials.

entries.before: Officials charged them with demonic speech; Your Highness pardoned their capital crime yet still barred them from court.
entries.after: The responsible officials memorialized that they spoke demonic words offending superiors and brought them to law; Your Highness, merciful and broad in acceptance, pardoned their capital offense yet still demoted, barred, and excluded them from court.
entries.sourceQuote: 主者奏以妖言犯上，至之于法，殿下慈弘苞納，恕其大辟，猶削黜禁錮，不齒於朝。
entries.sourceReason: 主者奏…至之于法, 慈弘苞納, and 削黜禁錮，不齒於朝 are under-covered by the shortened current en.

entries.before: To punish remonstrating ministers while seeking straight words is like going north to reach Yue!
entries.after: To punish remonstrating ministers while seeking straight words is like going north to reach Yue; how can there be any gain!
entries.sourceQuote: 罪諫臣而求直言，亦猶北行詣越，豈有得邪！
entries.sourceReason: 豈有得邪 completes the analogy and must not be dropped.

entries.before: Measure army and state needs, set posts, return the rest to farming, teach battle methods, and send students who fail after three years back to the fields; do not fill posts vainly and block worthy men.
entries.after: It is fitting to measure what army and state require, set the number of posts, and return the rest to farming; teach them battle methods; students who after three years have no achievement should also return to farming; they must not vainly fill the authorized establishment and block the path of the keen and worthy.
entries.sourceQuote: 宜量軍國所須，置其員數，已外歸之于農，教之戰法，學者三年無成，亦宜還之于農，不可徒充大員，以塞聰俊之路。
entries.sourceReason: 大員 here continues the quota/establishment sense, not an unspecified fill posts; keep the full sequential commands.

entries.before: It is fitting to measure what army and state require, set the number of posts, and return the rest to farming; teach them battle methods; students who after three years have no achievement should also return to farming; they must not vainly fill great posts and block the path of the keen and worthy.
entries.after: It is fitting to measure what army and state require, set the number of posts, and return the rest to farming; teach them battle methods; students who after three years have no achievement should also return to farming; they must not vainly fill the authorized establishment and block the path of the keen and worthy.
entries.sourceQuote: 宜量軍國所須，置其員數，已外歸之于農，教之戰法，學者三年無成，亦宜還之于農，不可徒充大員，以塞聰俊之路。
entries.sourceReason: 徒充大員 is vainly filling the authorized establishment/quotas, not great posts.

entries.before: if not, punish me, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
entries.after: if not, punish and execute me at once, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
entries.sourceQuote: 非也，登加罪戮，使天下知朝廷從善如流，罰惡不淹。
entries.sourceReason: 登加罪戮 calls for immediate punishment and execution of the speaker, not merely unspecified punishment.

entries.before: Agriculture is the foundation, yet magistrates ignore spring plowing—those who leave fields idle should face punishment to wake the commanderies.
entries.after: Agriculture is then the root of the state, yet two-thousand-bushel officials and county magistrates do not obey the first-month orders and do not urge lazy farmers; those especially who fail to open wasteland should be put under criminal law to awe and discipline the dependent cities.
entries.sourceQuote: 然則農者，國之本也，而二千石令長不遵孟春之令，惰農弗勸，宜以尤不修辟者措之刑法，肅厲屬城。
entries.sourceReason: 孟春之令, 惰農弗勸, 尤不修辟者, and 肅厲屬城 are missing from the compressed en.

entries.before: Then farming is the state’s root, yet two-thousand-bushel magistrates and county chiefs do not obey the first month’s orders, lazy farmers are not urged—ought with blame on those who do not cultivate wasteland apply to them criminal law, to awe and encourage dependent cities.
entries.after: Then farming is the state's root, yet two-thousand-bushel magistrates and county chiefs do not obey the first-month orders, and lazy farmers are not urged; those especially who do not open wasteland should be put under criminal law, to awe and discipline the dependent cities.
entries.sourceQuote: 然則農者，國之本也，而二千石令長不遵孟春之令，惰農弗勸，宜以尤不修辟者措之刑法，肅厲屬城。
entries.sourceReason: 尤不修辟者 means especially those who fail to open wasteland; with blame on those misreads 尤.

entries.before: Give each destitute household a draft ox.
entries.after: The poor who wholly lack assets and cannot support themselves shall each be granted one ox.
entries.sourceQuote: 貧者全無資產，不能自存，各賜牧牛一頭。
entries.sourceReason: 全無資產，不能自存 identifies the recipients; the bare grant leaves that description out without forcing a draft/herding label.

entries.before: Whoever wishes to rent state oxen and state land may do so under Wei–Jin precedent.
entries.after: If any have surplus private labor and gladly take official oxen to reclaim official fields, let them follow the old Wei and Jin rules.
entries.sourceQuote: 若私有餘力，樂取官牛墾官田者，其依魏、晉舊法。
entries.sourceReason: 私有餘力 and 墾官田 specify surplus labor reclaiming official fields under Wei-Jin rules.

entries.before: Dig irrigation works for public and private good—let engineers plan every channel.
entries.after: Irrigation ditches and channels benefit public and private interests; let the responsible officials plan and build them, striving to exhaust the advantages of water and land.
entries.sourceQuote: 溝洫溉灌，有益官私，主者量造，務盡水陸之勢。
entries.sourceReason: 主者 are responsible officials, not engineers, and 務盡水陸之勢 remains the construction aim.

entries.before: Wang Xian and Liu Ming although their crimes ought to be banned and dismissed, also is my lacking great measure.
entries.after: Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of great forbearance.
entries.sourceQuote: 王憲、劉明雖其罪應禁黜，亦猶孤之無大量也。
entries.sourceReason: 罪應禁黜 warrants ban and dismissal of the persons; saying crimes ought to be banned and dismissed misassigns the object.

entries.before: Feng Yu spoke as a true minister should.
entries.after: Master Feng is steadfastly upright and deeply embodies the character of a royal minister.
entries.sourceQuote: 封生蹇蹇，深得王臣之體。
entries.sourceReason: 封生蹇蹇，深得王臣之體 praises steadfast ministerial character; the thin current en drops both clauses.

entries.before: He tested students at the eastern school and promoted the best as attendants.
entries.after: Huang personally went to the eastern school to examine students; those whose command of the classics was thorough and outstanding were promoted to fill posts as close attendants.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝親臨東庠考試學生，其經通秀異者，擢充近侍。
entries.sourceReason: 經通秀異者 is the classical-proficiency criterion for promotion, not a bare the best.

entries.before: He remitted rent during a drought.
entries.after: Because of the prolonged drought, he remitted the common people's field rent.
entries.sourceQuote: 以久旱，丐百姓田租。
entries.sourceReason: Independent of the literal proposal, 久旱 and 百姓田租 require prolonged drought and commoners' field rent in en.

entries.before: He grouped refugees from Bohai, Hejian, Guangping, Wei, Donglai, Beihai, and Wu into new counties under Yan.
entries.after: He made the Bohai people into Xingji County, the Hejian people into Ningji County, the Guangping and Wei commandery people into Xingping County, the Donglai and Beihai people into Yuli County, and the Wu people into Wu County, all subordinate to the state of Yan.
entries.sourceQuote: 以勃海人為興集縣，河間人為寧集縣，廣平、魏郡人為興平縣，東萊、北海人為育黎縣，吳人為吳縣，悉隸燕國。
entries.sourceReason: Each settler group and its new county under Yan must be named; unnamed new counties omit those mappings.

entries.before: Again measure affairs to establish offices, measure offices to appoint men, so that offices match need and men do not hold empty posts; estimate yearly revenue and trim salaries accordingly.
entries.after: Again measure affairs to establish offices, measure offices to appoint men, so that offices match need and men do not hold empty posts; estimate the amount of annual revenue and determine their salaries accordingly.
entries.sourceQuote: 又量事置官，量官置人，使官必稱須，人不虛位，度歲入多少，裁而祿之。
entries.sourceReason: 裁而祿之 means determine remuneration in proportion to estimated annual income, not necessarily trim or cut salaries.

entries.before: Those who labor in the fields receive banners of distinction, while idle farmers suffer the penalty of being unranked.
entries.after: Those who labor in the fields receive rewards of public commendation and distinction, while idle farmers suffer the penalty of exclusion from standing among their peers.
entries.sourceQuote: 力田者受旌顯之賞，惰農者有不齒之罰。
entries.sourceReason: 旌顯 means publicly commend and distinguish; it does not specify a physical banner. 不齒 is exclusion from standing among one’s peers.

entries.before: Food must be taken from those who plow to feed others; one man eating the strength of one man, with tens of thousands idling, the loss is likewise; how can one achieve provision for every household and govern to peaceful ascendancy!
entries.after: Food must be taken from those who plow to feed them; one person consumes the labor of one person, and with tens of thousands living without working, the loss is likewise in the tens of thousands; how can every household be provided for and every person have enough, and government bring about peace!
entries.sourceQuote: 必取於耕者而食之，一人食一人之力，游食數萬，損亦如之，安可以家給人足，治致升平！
entries.sourceReason: 一人食一人之力 explicitly gives the one-to-one labor burden, 損亦如之 extends it to tens of thousands, and 家給人足 requires both household provision and personal sufficiency.

entries.before: If not, add punishment and execution, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
entries.after: If not, impose punishment and execution on me at once, so the realm knows the court follows good like flowing water and punishes evil without delay.
entries.sourceQuote: 非也，登加罪戮，使天下知朝廷從善如流，罰惡不淹。
entries.sourceReason: 登 adds immediacy to 加罪戮. The current literal includes execution but omits this explicit demand for prompt action.

entries.before: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
entries.after: He was carried back to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun to entrust him with affairs after his death.
entries.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
entries.sourceReason: 引俊屬以後事 describes summoning Jun and entrusting him with subsequent affairs, not merely briefing him on succession; 宮 is the palace, and 輦 specifies litter conveyance.

entries.before: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.
entries.after: He returned to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun, entrusting him with affairs after his death.
entries.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
entries.sourceReason: 引俊 here summons Jun; 屬以後事 entrusts him with the affairs to follow the dying ruler, as the next sentence confirms. Led Jun to entrust later affairs obscures who entrusts whom.

entries.before: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
entries.after: When Murong Jun assumed the imperial title in usurpation, he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wenming.
entries.sourceQuote: 俊僭號，追諡文明皇帝。
entries.sourceReason: 俊僭號 means Jun’s assumption of an imperial title, not his earlier succession to the throne. Preserve 僭 and avoid conflating the later imperial claim with succession after Huang’s death. The literal field already distinguishes this action.

entries.before: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
entries.after: Later he saw a white hare, galloped to shoot it; his horse fell and he was injured, then he told what he had seen.
entries.sourceQuote: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
entries.sourceReason: 後見白兔馳射之 is see then gallop-and-shoot, not merely charge; 乃說所見 narrates what was seen, not an omen gloss.

entries.before: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
entries.after: He died in the fourth year of Yonghe after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
entries.sourceQuote: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
entries.sourceReason: Chinese gives only 永和四年 with tenure and age; the western year 348 CE is not in the source sentence.

entries.before: Murong Han (defector general).
entries.after: Murong Han.
entries.sourceQuote: 慕容翰
entries.sourceReason: Unit is the bare personal-name heading 慕容翰; parenthetical defector general is editorial addition.

entries.before: He was bold, cunning, a superb archer, and immensely strong.
entries.after: He was heroic and bold, full of stratagems, ape-armed and skilled at archery, with strength that surpassed others.
entries.sourceQuote: 性雄豪，多權略，猿臂工射，膂力過人。
entries.sourceReason: 性雄豪多權略 needs heroic boldness and abundant stratagem, not cunning; 猿臂工射 must keep the ape-arms detail.

entries.before: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
entries.after: When he fled to Duan Liao, he was deeply respected and loved by Liao.
entries.sourceQuote: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
entries.sourceReason: 及奔段遼 states flight to Liao; 深為遼所敬愛 is deep respect and love, not merely honored after defection.

entries.before: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
entries.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to ride the victory and push deep; Murong Han, fearing this would bring harm on his native state, gave Lan deceitful counsel, and Lan then did not advance.
entries.sourceQuote: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入，翰慮成本國之害，詭說于蘭，蘭遂不進。
entries.sourceReason: Must keep 乘勝深入, 慮成本國之害, 詭說于蘭, and 蘭遂不進 as distinct propositions.

entries.before: Murong Huang’s host is elite.
entries.after: The King of Yan has come in person; his soldiers and horses are elite.
entries.sourceQuote: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。
entries.sourceReason: 燕王自來 is personal arrival of the Yan king; 士馬精銳 is elite troops and mounts, not host alone.

entries.before: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”
entries.after: Weapons are ill-omened tools, and battle holds peril; if you lose here, how will you defend the south?”
entries.sourceQuote: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」
entries.sourceReason: 兵者凶器 is the opening idiom and must be kept; 戰有危慮 and 何以南禦 close the warning.

entries.before: He chased Huang and was crushed.
entries.after: He then led his forces to pursue Huang, and Lan was indeed crushingly defeated.
entries.sourceQuote: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。
entries.sourceReason: 乃率眾追皝 states leading the host in pursuit; 蘭果大敗 marks the indeed-fulfilled great defeat.

entries.before: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.
entries.after: Although Murong Han dwelt in an enemy state, he established loyalty through the course of events—all cases were of this kind.
entries.sourceQuote: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。
entries.sourceReason: 因事立忠 is loyalty shown amid events, not secret work for Yan; 皆此類也 must remain as the summary.

entries.before: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.
entries.after: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.
entries.sourceQuote: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
entries.sourceReason: 既而逃 is Han’s flight before 歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之; both steps are required.

entries.before: You know my archery—do not force a fight.
entries.after: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.
entries.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
entries.sourceReason: 無為相逼自取死也 warns against pressing him and thereby seeking their own deaths; archery fame alone is incomplete.

entries.before: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.
entries.after: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
entries.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
entries.sourceReason: 相逼 is pressing the speaker, not forcing each other; 自取死也 is bringing death on yourselves.

entries.before: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;
entries.after: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;
entries.sourceQuote: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
entries.sourceReason: 吾射中者 means if the shot hits; 刀鐶 appears only in the next unit and should not be imported here.

entries.before: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.
entries.after: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.
entries.sourceQuote: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
entries.sourceReason: 後疾漸愈 and 騎馬自試 precede the denunciation; 私習騎 and 疑為非常 are report and suspicion, not a bare sedition gloss.

entries.before: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
entries.after: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
entries.sourceReason: 素忌之 is long jealousy or wariness; 賜死 is granting death, while poison is only stated later in 仰藥而死.

entries.before: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.
entries.after: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
entries.sourceReason: 素忌之 needs long-standing jealousy or wariness; plain envied is unclear wording for the same fact.

entries.before: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.
entries.after: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.
entries.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
entries.sourceReason: 罪不容誅 marks guilt beyond mere execution; 歸罪有司 is submitting to officials, after refusing 賊庭 bones.

entries.before: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.
entries.after: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
entries.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
entries.sourceReason: 歸罪有司 means submitting oneself to the authorities for punishment, not returning guilt onto them.

entries.before: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
entries.after: When Wang Jun held the province, Yu was transferred to administration aide; Jun was jealous and would not employ him.
entries.sourceQuote: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
entries.sourceReason: 轉治中從事 is the transfer; 忌而不能任 is jealousy plus refusal or failure to employ, not distrust alone.

entries.before: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
entries.after: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ them?"
entries.sourceQuote: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」
entries.sourceReason: Song has just named Liu Han and Yang Yu; 何以不任 refers to not employing them, not only him.

entries.before: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
entries.after: Cheng Pan replied, “Now Huaxia is split and crumbling, the nine provinces torn apart; where proper tracks reach is only as far as the Yi River.
entries.sourceQuote: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
entries.sourceReason: 軌跡所及易水而已 means civil order’s reach ends at the Yi, not that there is no refuge beyond it.

entries.before: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.
entries.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion (as in the “Kao pan”) and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
entries.sourceQuote: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
entries.sourceReason: 偃蹇考槃以待大通 is reclusive waiting for a great thaw; 俟河之清也 is the single impossibility simile, not a doubled clause.

entries.before: Let both sides forget old quarrels and restore peace so the realm stands firm as Taishan and the people can lay down their burdens.”
entries.after: Let both sides remedy their former faults and renew good faith as at the beginning, so the state may have the security of Mount Tai and the common people receive the blessing of laying down their burdens.”
entries.sourceQuote: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」
entries.sourceReason: 兩追前失 is remedy former faults, not forget quarrels; 通款如初 and 太山/息肩 images must stay.

entries.before: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.
entries.after: Murong Huang, who had long heard of Yu’s name, at once ordered his bonds released, appointed him Palace Director, then promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
entries.sourceReason: 素聞裕名 is long hearing of the name; offices are 郎中令 then 大將軍左司馬, not a vague senior major.

entries.before: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.
entries.after: Huang had long heard of Yu’s name; immediately ordered his bonds released; appointed Palace Director; promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
entries.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
entries.sourceReason: 素聞 needs had long heard; plain had heard is unclear, while the two office steps remain exact.

entries.before: Though he rose above older favorites, he lived modestly and treated everyone like a poor scholar.
entries.after: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
entries.sourceQuote: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
entries.sourceReason: Must keep 仕皝日近、寵秩在舊人之右, the virtue string 謙恭清儉剛簡慈篤, and 朝端若布衣之士.

entries.before: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”
entries.after: Earlier, Lu Chen of Fanyang always praised him, saying, “I have lived through Jin’s clear peace and have broadly observed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise and resolute, steadfast in faith and fierce in righteousness—men like Yang Shilun are in truth few.”
entries.sourceQuote: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
entries.sourceReason: Quote needs 晉之清平, the full 忠清簡毅篤信義烈 string, and courtesy name 陽士倫, not a thinned paraphrase.

entries.before: minister of the Duan
entries.after: served the Duan house
entries.sourceQuote: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
entries.sourceReason: 曆事段氏 means successively served the Duan house’s lords, not holding a post titled minister of the Duan.

entries.before: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s arrogance has peaked—now we can strike.”
entries.after: Huang said, “Moqian Hun’s extravagance and jealousy are already extreme; now then we can fight.”
entries.sourceQuote: 皝曰：「渾奢忌已甚，今則可一戰矣。」
entries.sourceReason: 奢忌 means extravagance and jealousy or suspicion, not arrogance; 今則可一戰矣 is now then one can fight, so the EN must not substitute a different charge.

entries.before: Sheyiyu is overrated and brittle—we must not let him sap our morale.”
entries.after: Sheyiyu vainly has an empty name; in truth he is easy to deal with; we ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.”
entries.sourceQuote: 奕于徒有虛名，其實易與耳，不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣。」
entries.sourceReason: 易與 means easy to deal with, not brittle, and 不宜縱敵挫吾兵氣 is ought not to loose the enemy and blunt our army’s spirit.

entries.before: Select agricultural officers with care, strive to the utmost in encouragement and assessment; each man tends a full hundred mu of field and does not borrow ox power;
entries.after: Select agricultural officers with care, strive to the utmost in encouragement and assessment; each man tends a full hundred mu of field and does not need ox power;
entries.sourceQuote: 高選農官，務盡勸課，人治周田百畝，亦不假牛力；
entries.sourceReason: 不假牛力 means not needing or relying on ox power. Restricting it to not borrowing that power leaves open reliance on one’s own oxen, which is not the assertion made here.

entries.before: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, for a thousand li no smoke rises; hunger and cold flow in ruin and men fall one after another into ditches and gullies.
entries.after: Since the Yongjia calamity the people have fled; the central plain is desolate, for a thousand li no smoke rises; people wander and perish from hunger and cold, falling one after another into ditches and gullies.
entries.sourceQuote: 自永嘉喪亂，百姓流亡，中原蕭條，千里無煙，饑寒流隕，相繼溝壑。
entries.sourceReason: 饑寒流隕 describes the displaced people wandering and perishing amid hunger and cold. Hunger and cold are not themselves the things that flow in ruin.

entries.before: Murong Hui, by divine martial strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; land was scarce and four in ten had no fields.
entries.after: Murong Hui, by divine martial prowess and sagacious strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign peoples beyond the frontier came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children returning to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; people were numerous, land was scarce, and four in ten had no fields.
entries.sourceQuote: 先王以神武聖略，保全一方，威以殄奸，德以懷遠，故九州之人，塞表殊類，繈負萬里，若赤子之歸慈父，流人之多舊土十倍有餘，人殷地狹，故無田者十有四焉。
entries.sourceReason: 塞表 explicitly places the foreign peoples beyond the frontier, and 神武聖略 and 人殷 separately state martial prowess, sagacious strategy, and the numerous population. The existing personal label is retained, not independently established or approved by this English review.

entries.before: Now households approach a hundred thousand, crowded narrow against the capital; I fear this will soon become a deep harm to the state; it is fitting to divide their brothers and lineage and move them to western border cities, soothe them with kindness and inspect them with law, so they do not scatter among settled people and learn the state's strength and weakness.
entries.after: Now households approach a hundred thousand, crowded narrow against the capital; I fear this will soon become a deep harm to the state; it is fitting to divide their brothers and lineage and move them to western border cities, soothe them with kindness and restrain them by law, so they do not scatter among settled people and learn the state's strength and weakness.
entries.sourceQuote: 今戶垂十萬，狹湊都城，恐方將為國家深害，宜分其兄弟宗屬，徙于西境諸城，撫之以恩，檢之以法，使不得散在居人，知國之虛實。
entries.sourceReason: 檢之以法 prescribes legal restraint or regulation of these populations, not inspection by means of law. The speaker’s fear and the two restrictions in the closing clause remain unchanged.

entries.before: Hunting parks all can be abolished, to give to common people without fields or occupations.
entries.after: The hunting parks can all be abolished and their land given to common people without farmland.
entries.sourceQuote: 苑囿悉可罷之，以給百姓無田業者。
entries.sourceReason: 田業 is farmland or landed livelihood in this land-distribution instruction, not a disjunction of lacking fields or lacking an occupation. The proposed correction preserves who receives the park land.

entries.before: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if I shoot the center, you then conveniently turn back;
entries.after: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
entries.sourceQuote: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
entries.sourceReason: 吾射中者 uses 中 as the verb “hit,” not a noun “center”; the literal must not read the hit as shooting the center.

entries.before: To hide and wait for peace is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
entries.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
entries.sourceQuote: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
entries.sourceReason: 偃蹇考槃以待大通 is proud reclusion awaiting a great opening, not merely hiding to wait for peace; both English fields needed the fuller propositions.

duplicateCurrentFieldFindings.alternativeAfter: Yet although orders to promote agriculture are repeatedly issued, none of the two-thousand-bushel administrators or magistrates is intent on diligent public service or keen to make full use of the land’s productive capacity.
